question.problem:
Find the median of the random variable $X$ if the probability density function of $X$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<1, \\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{{x}^{3}}},\, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The median of a random variable $X$ is the number $m$ such that

$$
P(X\le m)=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le m) & ={\int }_{1}^{m}\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{m}\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-3/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{x}^{-1/2}{|}_{1}^{m} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the median is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \sqrt{m} & =2 \\ m & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
